known_facts_book1: A girl sewn by Margolotte from a hundred-year-old patchwork quilt and stuffed with cotton-wadding, brought to life by Dr. Pipt's Powder of Life.
Has silver suspender-button eyes sewn on with black thread, gold-plate ears, brown yarn braids, pearl-bead teeth, a scarlet plush tongue and gold plates for finger-nails.
Her face patches are mismatched — one cheek yellow, the other red, chin blue, forehead purple, nose bright yellow — because Margolotte had no pink cloth.
Has far more brains than intended because Ojo secretly emptied every bottle on the Brain Furniture shelf into her dish, including a heavy dose of Cleverness.
Is named 'Scraps' by the Glass Cat; Margolotte had meant to call her 'Angeline'.
Speaks constantly in improvised nonsense verse, which the Glass Cat and Ojo take for craziness.
Cannot eat: her pearl teeth cannot chew and there is no opening beyond her mouth.
Has no heart and says so repeatedly, and would kill a dozen butterflies to help Ojo.
Was made to be Margolotte's servant, refuses to return to Dr. Pipt, and declares she will live in the Emerald City.
Takes the six-leaved clover from Ojo's basket and drops it into a golden vase in Dorothy's room, trying to destroy the evidence against him.
Shields Ojo from Chiss's shower of quills with her own body and is left full of holes, which a farm woman sews up.
Is thrown over the marble fence into the Horner Country, and negotiates with Chief Jak Horner to end the war.
Is declared by Ozma one of the curiosities of Oz, free to live where she pleases and nobody's servant but her own.
Is admired extravagantly by the Scarecrow, who calls her the most beautiful sight his eyes have ever beheld.

known_relations_book1.Margolotte: Her maker, who sewed and stuffed her to be a household servant.
known_relations_book1.Dr. Pipt: The magician who brought her to life and claims she belongs to him.
known_relations_book1.Ojo: Her first friend, whom she follows and defends and for whom she hides the clover.
known_relations_book1.Bungle: The Glass Cat, her constant sparring partner over which of them is more beautiful.
known_relations_book1.Scarecrow: Her great admirer, who is enchanted with her at first sight.
known_relations_book1.Jak Horner: The Horner Chief she bargains with to get the joke explained and the war called off.
known_relations_book1.the Woozy: A fellow travelling companion out of the Crooked Magician's country.

known_facts_book1: A cat made entirely of clear transparent glass by Dr. Pipt and brought to life by the first batch of the Powder of Life.
Has a mass of pink balls for brains that can be seen working, a blood-red ruby heart, two large emeralds for eyes and a spun-glass tail.
Says 'you can see 'em work' about her pink brains at nearly every opportunity, which everyone finds insufferable.
Refuses to catch mice, considering it undignified, and was named 'Bungle' by Margolotte.
Can see in the dark, and leads Ojo and Scraps along the path at night on a string tied round her neck.
Is unhurt by Chiss's quills, which rattle off her glass body without a scratch.
Refuses to go on the dangerous journey to the Quadling Country, preferring to stay safe at the palace.
Has her pink brains taken out by the Wizard and replaced with transparent ones, which makes her modest and well behaved.
Is kept in the palace as Ozma's pet at the end of the book.

known_facts_book1: A dark blue beast made all of squares and flat surfaces — square head, square body twice as long as wide, square stubby tail and four four-sided legs.
Is the only Woozy that has ever lived, in Oz or out of it.
Has no hair at all except exactly three stiff stubby hairs at the very tip of its tail, which no one can pull out.
Was fenced into a forest by Munchkin farmers because it ate up their honey-bees, and had eaten nothing for years until Ojo fed it bread and cheese.
Cannot be hurt: its skin is too thick and tough for anything to get through.
Flashes real fire from its eyes when angry, and is made angry by the word 'Krizzle-Kroo'; this is how it burns through the fence-board and escapes.
Believes its growl is the most terrible sound on earth, but the growl is only a small 'Quee-ee-ee-eek'.
Prides itself on being square, and therefore on always keeping its word.
Joins the party only because the three tail hairs cannot be pulled out and must be carried along inside the beast.
Is sent to the Royal Menagerie at the end of the book, with good care and plenty to eat for life.

known_facts_book1: A phonograph screwed fast to a small round table, brought to life by accident when the flung bottle scattered the Powder of Life over it.
Gives its name as 'Victor Columbia Edison'; Scraps shortens it to 'Vic' and Ojo calls it 'Phony'.
Runs away from Dr. Pipt, who threatened to smash it, and chases the travellers all night to catch up.
Owns one record: a classical composition on one side and a rag-time tune on the other, both of which the party find unbearable.
Cannot be stopped by throwing away the crank, which bounds back and rewinds the machine by itself.
Is driven off a second time after playing the popular song 'My Lulu', when the Shaggy Man threatens to take it apart and scatter its pieces.
Returns battered and scratched from having things thrown at it, and is not seen again after the Shaggy Man's threat.

known_relations_book1.Dr. Pipt: Its unwilling owner, who kicked it into a corner and threatened to smash it.
